title: Identification and Validation of BATF3 as a Promising Biomarker Gene for Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma.
authors: Zhu, Yidong; Liu, Jun; Zhang, Ting
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过机器学习与孟德尔随机化识别PTCL生物标志基因BATF3，但仅涉及基因表达与临床关联，未研究蛋白质-DNA互作或结合机制，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) is a rare and heterogeneous group of hematological malignancies. Treatment options are limited and often unsatisfactory, leading to a poor prognosis in most subtypes. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify potential biomarker genes for PTCL and to explore the underlying mechanisms by integrating machine learning, Mendelian Randomization (MR), and experimental validation. METHODS: Microarray datasets (GSE6338, GSE14879, and GSE59307) were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Differential expression analysis was conducted to identify the Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) between patients with PTCL and controls. A machine learning algorithm was then used to further refine the selection of characteristic genes for PTCL. We integrated genome-wide association studies data with expression quantitative trait loci data to identify genes with potential causal relationships to PTCL. Functional analysis was performed to explore underlying mechanisms. Finally, the identified gene was validated in clinical samples from patients with PTCL and controls. RESULTS: Based on 60 DEGs, the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithm identified nine characteristic genes for PTCL. MR analysis revealed 203 genes with causal effects on PTCL, ultimately identifying one co-expressed gene: Basic Leucine Zipper ATF-like Transcription Factor 3 (BATF3). It demonstrated good predictive performance across various PTCL subtypes, with AUC values ranging from 0.7 to 1. Functional analysis suggested that BATF3 may play a role in PTCL through immune- related pathways. Experimental validation using clinical samples further suggested the potential of this biomarker gene in PTCL. CONCLUSION: By combining machine learning, MR, and experimental validation, we identified and validated BATF3 as a promising biomarker of PTCL. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying PTCL and may inform the development of effective treatment strategies for this disease.
abstract_zh: 背景：外周T细胞淋巴瘤（PTCL）是一种罕见且异质性强的血液恶性肿瘤。治疗选择有限且常不尽如人意，导致大多数亚型预后不良。目的：本研究旨在通过整合机器学习、孟德尔随机化（MR）及实验验证，识别PTCL的潜在生物标志物基因，并探讨其潜在机制。方法：从基因表达综合数据库下载微阵列数据集（GSE6338、GSE14879和GSE59307）。进行差异表达分析，以识别PTCL患者与对照组之间的差异表达基因（DEGs）。随后使用机器学习算法进一步筛选PTCL的特征基因。我们将全基因组关联研究数据与表达数量性状位点数据整合，以识别与PTCL具有潜在因果关系的基因。进行功能分析以探讨潜在机制。最后，在PTCL患者和对照组的临床样本中验证所识别的基因。结果：基于60个DEGs，最小绝对收缩和选择算子算法识别出九个PTCL特征基因。MR分析揭示了203个对PTCL具有因果效应的基因，最终确定一个共表达基因：碱性亮氨酸拉链ATF样转录因子3（BATF3）。该基因在不同PTCL亚型中表现出良好的预测性能，AUC值范围为0.7至1。功能分析提示BATF3可能通过免疫相关通路在PTCL中发挥作用。使用临床样本的实验验证进一步提示了该生物标志物基因在PTCL中的潜力。结论：通过结合机器学习、MR和实验验证，我们识别并验证了BATF3作为PTCL的有前景的生物标志物。这些发现为PTCL的分子机制提供了见解，并可能为该疾病的有效治疗策略开发提供信息。
